 :J U D G M E N T:
This is a claim petition U/Sec.163-A of MV Act claiming compensation of Rs.10,00,000/- with interest for the injuries suffered in the Motor Vehicle Accident occurred on 02.03.2018.
2. The averments of the petition is brief is as follows:
On 02.03.2018 at about 8.00 p.m., the petitioner was proceeding by riding the Motorcycle bearing Reg.No.AP-04-AU- 3443.

When the petitioner reached near Vijayanagaram Colony at Gurram Venkata Ramaiah field, Rayachoty, at that time another Motorcycle bearing Reg.No.AP-04-BC-9321 being driven by its rider from opposite direction with high speed and dashed petitioner's motorcycle.

As a result,
the petitioner sustained grievous injuries such as head injury, left frontal contusions with relatively dilated left frontal horn, occipital region, left radius fracture, ACF floor fracture and other multiple injuries.

Immediately, the petitioner was shifted to Government Hospital, Kadapa and then he was shifted to Narayanadri Hospital, Tirupati and then to C.M.C. Hospital, Vellore and admitted as an inpatient for one month.
The doctor has advised him to take bed rest and undergone periodical checkup.
Due to injuries sustained in the accident, the face of petitioner became disfigured and he lost memory power, self control and concentration.
Due to head injury, the petitioner getting headache and giddiness.
Due to radius fracture, the petitioner cannot hold, raise and lift weight.
Due to permanent disability sustained by the petitioner, he cannot do his day to day work.
The petitioner was 38 years at the time of accident, by doing carpenter work he was earning Rs.3,300/- per month.
Due to permanent disability sustained by the petitioner, he is idle without doing any work.
The accident was occurred due to involvement of both motor cycles bearing Reg.No.AP-04-AU-3443 and AP-04-BC- 9321 and in this regard, the Rayachoty police have registered the case.
The R.C. owner cum driver of the motor cycle bearing Reg.No.AP-04-BC-9321 was died in the same accident and his L.R., his father Avatala Ramanjula Reddy has been arrayed as respondent No.1.
With these averments he prayed to award compensation.

sentences.text: 3. After service of notice, 2nd respondent-Insurance company appeared through it's counsel and filed written statement.

In so far as 1st respondent i.e., L.R. of R.C. owner of offending vehicle is concerned, he remained absent and he has been placed Ex-parte.
4. The written statement averments of the 2nd respondent are hereunder:

The 2nd respondent has admitted the issuance of insurance policy with respect to Motor Cycle bearing Reg.No.AP-04-BC-9321 and contended that, the liability is subject to the terms and conditions of the policy.
It is contended that, there is no negligence on the part of the rider of insured vehicle as he was proceeding with due care and caution.
On the contrary the accident caused due to sole negligence of the petitioner, who was riding the motor cycle bearing Reg.No.AP-04-AU-3443 without wearing helmet.
The police have filed the charge sheet against the petitioner.
The 2nd respondent has denied the age, occupation, income, injuries sustained by the petitioner and amount spent towards medical expenses.

The 2nd respondent has contended that, the insured has violated the mandatory provisions under Sec.134(c)
of M.V.Act by not submitting the vehicle document.
The police have also violated the mandatory provisions of under Sec.158(6) of M.V. Act.
Hence, prayed to dismiss the petition.

5. On the basis of the above pleadings, the predecessor in the office has framed the following :ISSUES:
1.

Whether the petitioner proves that he sustained injuries on account of rash and negligent riding of motor cycle bearing registration No.AP-04-BC-9321 by its rider on 02.03.2018 as contended in the petition?

2. Whether the petitioner proves that, he is entitled for the compensation? If so, to what extent and from whom?
3. Whether Respondent No.2 proves alleged contributory negligence on the part of Petitioner?
4. What order or award?

6. It is relevant to note that, the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Shivaji and Another Vs. Divisional Manager, United India Insurance Co. Ltd., and Others reported in AIR 2018 SC 3705 held that, "in a proceeding under Sec.163-A of the Act, the insurer cannot raise any defence of negligence on the part of the victim to counter a claim for compensation".

3 Whether the petitioner proves that he has sustained injuries in an accident occurred on 02.03.2018 as contended in the petition?
7. In order to prove the case, the petitioner examined himself as P.W.1 and marked Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.9.
Further, he examined two witnesses namely S. Eswar Reddy and Jaya Raj Y., as P.W.2 and P.W.3.
Ex.P.10 to Ex.P.15 were marked through P.W.2 and Ex.P.16 to Ex.P.18 were marked through P.W.3.
Respondent No.2 has not adduced any evidence.
P.W.1 to P.W.3 were cross-
examined from the side of respondent No.2.
8. Heard the arguments from both side.
Perused the records placed before the Tribunal.

The findings of this Tribunal to the above referred Issues are as under:-
Recasted Issue No.1 :- In the Affirmative.
Issue No.2 :- In the Partly Affirmative.
Issue No.3 :- Answered accordingly.
9. RECASTED ISSUE No.1 and ISSUE No.3:-
Before going to discuss Issue No.1, it is appropriate to take Issue No.3 for discussion here itself.
In the instant case, the petitioner has pleaded that, he has sustained injuries in the road accident.

However,
the 2nd respondent-Insurance company contended the rash or negligence and also contended the contributory negligence on the side of petitioner.

Again at the cost of repetition, it is worth to rely on the decision of Hon'ble Apex Court held in the case of Shivaji and Another Vs. Divisional Manager, United India Insurance Co. Ltd., and Others reported in AIR 2018 SC 3705 held that, "in a proceeding under Sec.163-A of the Act, the insurer cannot raise any defence of negligence on the part of the victim to counter a claim for compensation".

sentences.text:
As per the decision of Hon'ble Apex Court referred supra, it is crystal clear that, in a proceedings under Sec.163-A of M.V. Act,
the 2 nd respondent cannot raise any defence of negligence on the part of petitioner.

Further, it is worth to rely on the decision reported in 2012 ACJ 1335 in a case of United India Insurance Co. Ltd., Vs. Mohanan and others, wherein it is held that, "the contention that, deceased was responsible for accident not sustainable, claim petition under 163-A of Act is maintainable.
Negligence is irrelevant in claim petition filed under Sec.163-A and when negligence is irrelevant,

entities.text: United India Insurance Co. Ltd., Vs. Mohanan and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: contributory negligence is also irrelevant".
Therefore, it is well settled legal position of law that, in a claim petition under Sec.163-A of M.V. Act, negligence or fault is irrelevant.
Therefore, Issue No.3 is answered accordingly.

sentences.text: In order to prove the case, the petitioner has examined himself as P.W.1 by way of filing affidavit in support of his oral examination-in-chief.
Hence, this Tribunal need not to recapitulate the same once again at this juncture.
P.W.1 has relied on Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.4.
Accordingly, Ex.P.1 is the true copy of FIR pertaining to Cr.No.253/2018.
Ex . P.2
is the true copy of Complaint in Telugu language.
Ex.P.2(a) is the English translated copy of complaint.
Ex . P.3
is the true copy of wound certificate.
Ex.P.4 is the true copy of charge sheet.
11. As per Ex.P.1, FIR was registered before the Rayachoty police station.
Likewise charge sheet was also filed against the petitioner himself.
Therefore, there is no dispute with respect to injuries caused to the petitioner in the road accident.
Accordingly, recasted Issue No.1 is answered in the Affirmative.
12. ISSUE No.2:- This issue is with respect to entitlement of relief.

At this juncture it is worth to refer the decision of our Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka reported in 2004 ACJ 1289 between Appaji Vs. M. Krishna, the Hon'ble Division Bench held that, "non obstant clause in Sec.163-A dispenses with proof of fault by claimants against the driver or owner of vehicle involved in the accident.

entities.text: High Court of Karnataka reported in 2004 ACJ 1289
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: So there is no liability on claimant to prove negligence or rashness of other party.
However, if at all the accident is caused on account of his own rash and negligent driving, it can neverthless make the insurnace company pay for the same".
The above referred decision is aptly applicable to the case on hand.
13. Learned counsel for the petitioner would submit that, the petitioner has incurred Rs.78,883.50 towards medical expenses and he is entitled for the same.
He also submit that, the petitioner was earning Rs.3,330/- per month.
Due to his disability, he could not earn.

Per-contra, learned counsel for the 2nd respondent would submit that, as per II Schedule of M.V. Act, the petitioner is entitled for Rs.5,000/- under the head of pain and sufferings if the injuries are grievous in nature and Rs.1,000/- if the injuries are non-grievous in nature.
Further argued that, the petitioner is entitled for Rs.15,000/- towards medical expenses.
In the instant case, the petitioner has not examined the doctor to prove his disability.
Further, as per Ex.P.7, the petitioner incurred Rs.78,883.50 towards medical expenses.
As per Ex.P.3, the injuries are shown as grievous in nature.

As per II schedule of M.V. Act, the petitioner is entitled for Rs.15,000/- towards medical expenses and Rs.5,000/-
towards pain and sufferings.
Hence, this Tribunal is of the view that, the petitioner is entitled for Rs.20,000/- as compensation.
14. Regarding liability and interest.
There is no dispute with regard to issuance of insurance policy to the offending vehicle.
In view of the decision reported in MFA NO: 30131-2019 dtd, 12.5.2020 rate of interest on the compensation amount is awarded at 6% p.a. from the date of petition.
Accordingly, Issue No.2 is answered in the partly affirmative.
15. ISSUE No.4:-
In view of discussions referred to above, this Tribunal proceed to pass the following.

5 :ORDER:
Claim Petition filed by the Petitioner U/Sec.163-A of M.V. Act is partly allowed with costs of the Petition.
Petitioner is awarded just and reasonable compensation of Rs.20,000/- (Rupees Twenty Thousand only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a., from the date of petition to till the date of depositing of the compensation amount in the Tribunal.
Respondent No.2 shall deposit the compensation in the court within 2 months from the date of this judgment.
Advocate's fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw Award Accordingly.
:APPORTIONMENT:
Scheme of investment is dispensed with as amount awarded is too meager.
